notes: The Home Depot (homedepot.com). ACCESS: robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (checked before any bypass). Homepage, all sitemap XML files, and /daily-deals fetch cleanly today via direct curl_cffi HTTP (chrome124/safari17_0 impersonation, tier 1) and via headless Playwright with a real Chrome fingerprint (tier 2). However every /b/ (catalog/category), /c/ (content/article), and /s/ (site search) path returns a consistent Akamai-edge 403 ('Error Page', 2414 bytes) under BOTH tier 1 and tier 2, confirming the prior Home-Decor pass's finding that the block is scoped to catalog/content/search paths, not the whole origin, and is not a simple UA check (a real headless-browser fingerprint still gets 403). Given this reproducible pattern I did not escalate to Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3), since browser selection there requires interactive user confirmation which this synchronous worker cannot perform, and tier 1+2 already gave a thorough, well-supported absence answer using legitimate site data (see below) rather than an access failure. DISCOVERY PERFORMED: (1) parsed the full current core-taxonomy sitemap (https://www.homedepot.com/sitemap/B/PLPs/PLP_CORE_TAX/PLP_CORE_TAX-0.xml, 5,287 unfaceted category nodes) for Bestsellers/Best-Sellers/Top-Sellers/Trending/Popular/Customer-Favorites keywords - zero hits; (2) sampled the 44 PLP_REFINED (faceted) sitemap shards (0,5,15,25,35,42; ~45,000 URLs each) - the only recurring hit is a 'Trending' facet VALUE (code Z1z26b4f) that always appears stacked on top of an already-narrowed leaf category (e.g. Kitchen-Kitchen-Faucets/.../Trending, Hardware-Cabinet-Hardware/Matte/Trending, Bath/Best-Rated/Trending) - this is an in-category sort/filter refinement, never a standalone bare-department 'Trending' or 'Best Sellers' page, so it is excluded per the brief's 'arbitrary filter page' rule; (3) parsed the Collections sitemap (3,533 curated single-product-family pages) - only 1 'best-seller' hit and it's a single-brand cleaning-product family page (Odoban), not decor-relevant and not a genuine site-wide Bestsellers PLP; (4) inspected the rendered homepage's embedded Apollo state: it contains a 'Best Sellers' product-shelf widget with a hardcoded list of 24 SKUs and navParam:null - i.e. it is a curated homepage carousel with NO dedicated PLP URL of its own, so per brief section 3 (a listing must be an actual openable PLP) it does not qualify as a row; (5) checked the homepage 'Shop by Category' flyout tiles (full list extracted from embedded JSON) - only Labor Day Savings, Daily Deals, and Special Savings (generic promo hub) plus the 18 straight department links; none is Bestsellers-named; (6) opened /daily-deals directly (200, real content) - it is a temporary 'Deals of the Day' promo landing page built from several separately-themed shelves ('Deals of the Day', 'Popular Picks', 'Top Rated') with no single exact product count and no site-taxonomy Bestsellers labeling - excluded as promotional, not a Bestsellers PLP; (7) attempted the site's own search (/s/bestsellers) - blocked 403 (see ACCESS above), so search could not be used as supporting evidence, but this does not change the taxonomy-based absence finding since the taxonomy sitemap is the authoritative full current catalog structure. CONCLUSION: no genuine Bestsellers/Top-Sellers/Trending-as-a-PLP/Customer-Favorites listing exists anywhere in Home Depot's current taxonomy, homepage nav, or promotional shelving that meets the brief's definition of a standalone PLP. Caveat: because /b/ department landing pages (e.g. /b/Home-Decor, /b/Lighting) are blocked outright, I could not directly rule out a department-page-embedded 'Best Sellers' shelf analogous to the homepage's (which, per point 4, would not qualify as its own PLP row anyway since it lacks an independent URL) - this is a residual access gap, not a contradiction of the absence finding.
